subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should `sessions_spawn` select only configured bounded lane classes under a global sub-agent ceiling, or should isolation derive from agent identity or queue priority without a new lane parameter?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but the permanent tool and config contract determines resource isolation, starvation, lane cardinality, and operator control; prior arbitrary-lane attempts show these are product decisions rather than a mechanical patch.

options.title: Bounded configured classes
options.body: Allow `sessions_spawn` to choose only declared lane classes, each capped beneath a preserved aggregate sub-agent limit.

options.title: Identity-derived isolation
options.body: Assign lanes from parent or target agent configuration and keep arbitrary lane selection out of the model-facing tool.

options.title: Priority-only scheduling
options.body: Keep one sub-agent lane and add priorities, visibility, or per-parent limits instead of independent pools.

recommendation.title: Bounded configured classes
recommendation.body: Allow `sessions_spawn` to choose only declared lane classes, each capped beneath a preserved aggregate sub-agent limit.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature and concurrency history most strongly routes through the original `sessions_spawn` and agent-limit work.
